models.question: Once a normal (fuel-from-burner) spherical gas flame is lit, does it go out on its own (radiative self-extinction) before the scripted timeout?
models.target_definition: 1 if extinction_mode == 'self_extinguished', 0 if 'flow_terminated' at the script timeout; flames stopped by the burner temperature limit (per the test sheets) are left out

features.name: x_o2_ambient
features.why: more O2 raises T_f and heat release relative to radiation

features.name: pressure_kpa
features.why: soot and gas radiation grow with pressure

features.name: fuel_flow_mg_s
features.why: flame radius grows with fuel flow, radiative loss ~ r_f^3 against heat release ~ mdot, so chi_r rises

features.name: fuel_fraction
features.why: dilution lowers T_ad (favours extinction) but also lowers soot (favours survival)

features.name: n_carbon
features.why: larger alkanes soot more

training_filter.why: no established hot flame (ignited False): there is nothing to extinguish (21106 F4 is kept: the table logs it as not ignited, the raw data show a 20 s flame, patch D03)
no recorded outcome

stopped by the burner temperature limit according to the test sheet (out = temp_limit, note patch D58; the sheet values are an AI reading of hand-filled scans, not checked by a human): the flame was cut off early, so whether it would have gone out by itself is not known

models.interpretation: Partly, and weakly. Ambient O2 (-) agrees with an interval excluding 0 and carries the model. Fuel flow (+, larger flame, more radiative loss) agrees, but its interval only just excludes 0. Pressure and carbon number are indistinguishable from 0 (pressure has the opposite sign to the expectation). On held-out days the model is barely better than its single best feature (AUC 0.69 against 0.67) and than the base rate (Brier 0.129 against 0.135), and the range of its AUC when the test days are resampled (0.36-0.80) includes chance; the depth-3 tree and gradient boosting do no better. With the 12 flames stopped by the burner temperature limit counted as 'did not self-extinguish' the AUC was 0.84: part of that score came from flames whose outcome is not known. Read the probabilities as a description of these tests (19 flames reached the timeout, 18 of them at about 40% O2).
caveats: 'Flow-terminated' is not 'stable': the negatives are flames still burning at the scripted timeout, so the target is 'self-extinguished before the timeout', and the fractions depend on the chosen timeouts.

The 12 flames stopped by the burner temperature limit are left out: they were cut off early, so whether they would have gone out is not known. They are taken from the hand-filled test sheets (out = temp_limit, note patch D58), an AI reading of scans that nobody checked; the table logs them as flow_terminated like the timeouts. A misread tick would move a flame in or out of the fit. Leaving them out removes the hottest burns (11 of the 12 carry burner_over_limit), so the model says nothing about conditions that overheat the burner.
At about 21% ambient O2 every lit flame self-extinguished (quasi-complete separation); the coefficients mainly describe the about 40% O2 tests. Only 2 tests sit at about 33% O2.
Chamber composition drifts during a day (closed chamber); x_o2_ambient is the tabulated estimate, not a gas-chromatograph measurement. Mass flow controllers are poor below 10% of full scale.
Burner temperature (which lengthens burns) is not a feature: it is an outcome of the burn.
must_not_be_used_for: material flammability, cabin fires or condensed fuels
other burners or flow timeouts (the target is tied to this hardware's cut-off times)
O2 between 0.25 and 0.35 (2 tests) or any combination not near a listed nearest test

models.question: Once an inverse (oxidiser-from-burner, fuel ambient) flame is lit, does it self-extinguish before the scripted timeout, and how strongly does chamber pressure matter?
models.target_definition: 1 if extinction_mode == 'self_extinguished', 0 if 'flow_terminated' at the script timeout (usually 66 s for inverse flames); flames stopped by the burner temperature limit (per the test sheets) are left out

features.name: pressure_kpa
features.why: soot forms outside the inverse flame in the hot fuel-rich gas; radiation grows with pressure

features.name: x_o2_burner
features.why: more O2 in the burner stream raises T_ad

features.name: o2_flow_mg_s
features.why: O2 is the limiting reactant, so O2 flow sets the flame size and hence radiative loss

features.name: n_carbon
features.why: larger alkanes soot more

training_filter.why: flash_only: a ~1 s momentary flame is a failed ignition, not a radiative extinction of an established flame
no hot ignition
no recorded outcome

stopped by the burner temperature limit according to the test sheet (out = temp_limit, note patch D58; the sheet values are an AI reading of hand-filled scans, not checked by a human): the flame was cut off early, so whether it would have gone out by itself is not known

models.interpretation: Pressure agrees strongly (+) and is the largest term (a pressure split alone gives a pooled held-out AUC of 0.71 against 0.90 for the full model; gradient boosting does no better on held-out days), matching 0/20 self-extinctions at 0.5-0.6 bar against 58/67 at 2.2-3.3 bar. Burner-stream O2 has the opposite sign to the a-priori expectation (-): richer oxidiser streams self-extinguished more often. This is a property of the test design, not a mechanism: the O2 mass flow was held roughly fixed, so a richer burner stream means a smaller total burner flow (correlation about -0.66 between burner O2 and the log of the estimated total flow). The sign stays positive within each pressure level and with day fixed effects, and it becomes indistinguishable from 0 once total flow replaces O2 flow, so the data cannot separate burner O2 from total flow. O2 flow and carbon number are indistinguishable from 0.
caveats: All inverse rows carry pressure_9pct_above_nominal: the table pressures are ~9% above the fill levels. Used as given: a uniform multiplicative offset only shifts the intercept of log10(pressure).
Pressure and O2 flow are partly confounded with test day: pressure levels were run on separate days, so the grouped CV can only test pressure on held-out days with other pressures.
79 of 154 inverse tests used 85% O2 in the burner stream; low burner-O2 cells are small.

Ambient fuel fraction is left out: it was lowered as pressure was raised (r = -0.73 with pressure in the training rows), so the two cannot be separated and the fit would split the pressure effect between them.
As for normal flames, 'flow_terminated' is a timeout outcome, not a stability limit.

The 12 flames stopped by the burner temperature limit are left out: they were cut off early, so whether they would have gone out is not known. They are taken from the hand-filled test sheets (out = temp_limit, note patch D58), an AI reading of scans that nobody checked; the table logs them as flow_terminated like the timeouts, and the sheet of 21270 A4 itself asks whether it timed out. Nine of the 12 were at 0.5-0.6 bar, where 20 flames remain, all of them reaching the timeout.
must_not_be_used_for: normal flames or real fires (an inverse flame has no fire-safety analogue in a cabin)
pressures outside 0.5-3.3 bar or other burners

models.question: Does a normal flame light (hot ignition) for a given chamber O2, pressure and fuel stream?
models.target_definition: 1 if the table's 'Hot ignition' is yes, 0 if no (rows that were not ignition attempts, patches D45-D50, excluded)

features.name: x_o2_ambient
features.why: faster chemistry and hotter flame (Damköhler number up)

features.name: pressure_kpa
features.why: reaction rate ~ p^n with n ~ 2 for chain branching, so Da rises

features.name: fuel_flow_mg_s
features.why: more fuel near the igniter

features.name: fuel_fraction
features.why: heavily diluted fuel gives a cool, weak mixture near the igniter

features.name: n_carbon
features.why: no clear expectation across C2-C4 alkanes

training_filter.why: ignition outcome not recorded
not an ignition attempt (patches D45-D50: no fuel or no oxidizer flowed, or the run was aborted before gas flow); the table lists the row as not ignited
zero fuel fraction or zero fuel flow: no fuel was supplied

models.interpretation: O2 agrees (+, interval excludes 0); pressure, flow and dilution agree in sign only. The robust statement is the dilution table: 14/37 ignitions below 0.05 fuel fraction against 119/139 above. The fit does not generalise to held-out days (grouped AUC near chance), because the failures cluster on a few days with modified igniter settings.
caveats: Igniter energy was deliberately lowered in some tests to try direct cool-flame ignition (final report); igniter settings are not in the table, so some failures are by design and look like condition effects.
Mass flow controllers are poor below 10% of full scale, which is where most diluted, low-flow failures sit.
Failures cluster by day: all 43 fall on 6 of 11 test days (12 Apr - 11 Jun 2021), 42 of them on 5, and the grouped CV (held-out days) is close to chance. Kept as a descriptive table, not a predictor.
must_not_be_used_for: flammability limits of materials or of premixed gases
igniters other than the ACME hot-wire igniter at standard settings

models.question: Does an inverse flame light, given the burner-stream O2 and chamber pressure?
models.target_definition: 1 if 'Hot ignition' is yes, 0 if no ('flash' rows and rows that were not ignition attempts, patches D45-D50, excluded)

features.name: x_o2_burner
features.why: a richer oxidiser stream gives a hotter, faster-reacting mixture at the igniter

features.name: pressure_kpa
features.why: Da rises with pressure

training_filter.why: flash_only: momentary flame, neither a clean ignition nor a failure
ignition outcome not recorded
not an ignition attempt (patches D45-D50: no fuel or no oxidizer flowed, or the run was aborted before gas flow); the table lists the row as not ignited

tree_rules.decision_tree_depth3:
|--- x_o2_burner <= 0.255
|   |--- log10(pressure_kpa) <= 1.892
|   |   |--- class: 0
|   |--- log10(pressure_kpa) >  1.892
|   |   |--- log10(pressure_kpa) <= 2.432
|   |   |   |--- class: 1
|   |   |--- log10(pressure_kpa) >  2.432
|   |   |   |--- class: 1
|--- x_o2_burner >  0.255
|   |--- x_o2_burner <= 0.350
|   |   |--- class: 1
|   |--- x_o2_burner >  0.350
|   |   |--- log10(pressure_kpa) <= 2.193
|   |   |   |--- class: 1
|   |   |--- log10(pressure_kpa) >  2.193
|   |   |   |--- class: 1

models.interpretation: Burner O2 agrees (+) on average, but the table shows the effect is not monotone: the failures concentrate at 0.21 burner O2, while the few lower-O2 tests mostly lit.
caveats: Only 12 non-ignitions, 9 of them at 0.21 burner O2; the fit is close to a lookup of that cell. Read the descriptive table first.
Igniter settings varied and are not in the table.
Not monotone in burner O2: 6 of 7 tests at 0.12-0.19 ignited while 9 of 25 at 0.21 failed, so a logistic curve in O2 misdescribes the low end. Kept as a descriptive table.

models.question: How fast does a free methanol or n-heptane droplet burn (d²-law constant K) in a given atmosphere?
models.target_definition: average burning-rate constant K (mm²/s) of the d²-law d² = d0² - K t, as tabulated

features.name: is_heptane
features.why: heptane has the larger transfer number B

features.name: x_o2_ambient
features.why: B grows with ambient O2

features.name: x_co2
features.why: CO2's heat capacity lowers T_f and B

features.name: x_he
features.why: helium raises the gas conductivity lambda

features.name: pressure_kpa
features.why: quasi-steady theory: K nearly independent of pressure

features.name: d0_mm
features.why: radiative loss grows with droplet and flame size; small methanol droplets burn faster than predicted

training_filter.why: no burning-rate constant
no initial diameter or pressure (includes C11M201, pressure_zero_in_source)
composition_sum: O2/N2/CO2/He fractions (features) sum to 0.98
duplicate_id: the two 193F001 rows disagree on d0, K and burn time

prediction_interval.method: 5th-95th percentile of grouped out-of-fold residuals, added to the prediction
prediction_interval.method_plain: The model is refitted without each group of test days and its error on those days is recorded; the range is the estimate plus the 5th and 95th percentile of those errors.

held_out_coverage.method: nested grouped cross-validation: each held-out day's range is rebuilt from the other days only

sensitivity.without: the tests that went out early (D_ext/D0 > 0.9), where K is fitted over a short burn

models.interpretation: Yes, every term with an expectation agrees and its interval excludes 0: K rises with O2 and helium (conductivity), falls with CO2 and with initial diameter (radiative loss), and is slightly higher for heptane. Pressure has a small positive coefficient that is not robust: it shrinks about fourfold when the tests that went out early are left out (see Sensitivity), so K is best read as independent of pressure here, as quasi-steady theory says. The linear model beats gradient boosting on held-out days (R² 0.69 vs 0.53), so there is no evidence of missed non-linearity.
caveats: The rows include tests that went out early (D_ext/D0 > 0.9). They are kept, because leaving them out would select on the outcome, but the pressure coefficient depends on them (see Sensitivity).
K is one average per test; the tabulated value is not accompanied by the diameter history it came from.
Needle conformal-coating contamination (2009-2011) is judged by the team to affect K minimally.
Diluent fractions vary jointly (O2/N2/CO2/He sum to 1), so coefficients are partial effects at fixed remaining fractions; N2 is the implicit reference.
must_not_be_used_for: other fuels, fibre-supported droplets or sprays
predicting whether a droplet ignites (no failed-ignition rows exist)
burn time (needs the extinction diameter, which this model does not predict)

models.question: At what droplet diameter does a burning methanol droplet go out?
models.target_definition: visible-flame extinction diameter (mm), tests that ended in flame extinction

features.name: d0_mm
features.why: absorbed product water accumulates to ~30% of the droplet mass, so D_ext grows roughly linearly with D0

features.name: x_o2_ambient
features.why: diffusive (Damköhler) extinction diameter grows as O2 falls

features.name: x_co2
features.why: the team reports D_ext nearly independent of diluent type

features.name: x_he
features.why: as for CO2

features.name: pressure_kpa
features.why: no clear expectation over 0.7-3 atm

training_filter.why: not methanol (heptane mixes radiative and diffusive branches)
test ended by disruption or completion, not extinction
ext_zero / ext_gt_d0: extinction diameter (the target) is a placeholder or impossible
no extinction diameter, initial diameter or pressure
composition_sum: ambient fractions (features) sum to 0.98
duplicate_id: the two 193F001 rows disagree

prediction_interval.method: 5th-95th percentile of grouped out-of-fold residuals, added to the prediction
prediction_interval.method_plain: The model is refitted without each group of test days and its error on those days is recorded; the range is the estimate plus the 5th and 95th percentile of those errors.

held_out_coverage.method: nested grouped cross-validation: each held-out day's range is rebuilt from the other days only

models.interpretation: Yes. D_ext grows with D0 (0.82 mm per mm, close to the linear water-absorption scaling) and with lower O2. CO2 and helium both enlarge D_ext; that is consistent with the Damköhler picture (CO2 lowers T_f and slows chemistry; helium's higher diffusivity shortens the residence time d_f²/α), though the team describes D_ext as nearly independent of diluent. Gradient boosting is only slightly better (R² 0.74 vs 0.70).
caveats: Rows mix diffusive and (below ~14% O2) radiative extinctions; the table does not label which.
Some extinction diameters were extrapolated when the droplet drifted out of view.
Disrupted droplets (often from needle-coating contamination) are excluded, which selects cleaner tests.
must_not_be_used_for: an oxygen index (LOI) estimate: no failed-ignition rows exist

models.question: At 2-5 atm, does an n-dodecane (or n-/iso-dodecane blend) droplet re-ignite a hot flame from its cool flame after the first radiative extinction?

features.name: pressure_kpa
features.why: low-temperature chemistry and heat release rise with pressure

features.name: d0_mm
features.why: a larger droplet leaves more fuel and a longer cool-flame phase

features.name: iso_dodecane_fraction
features.unit: mole fraction of iso-dodecane in the fuel
features.why: branched iso-dodecane suppresses low-temperature chemistry

features.name: x_he
features.why: helium shortens hot flames but the team reports it helps the heat-release/heat-loss balance in the NTC region

features.name: x_o2_ambient
features.why: more O2, more vigorous cool-flame chemistry

training_filter.why: not analysed in the data-summary spreadsheet (all farnesane, untested points)
no initial diameter
composition_sum: O2 + N2 = 0.97 (FLEX-1219 to 1222)
below 2 atm: 0 re-ignitions in every analysed test (see the descriptive table); a logistic fit across that wall is pure separation

models.interpretation: Pressure agrees (+) and is the only effect: none of 86 analysed tests at or below 1.25 atm re-ignited, against 36 of 62 at 2-5 atm. Within 2-5 atm nothing else is resolvable; d0 has the opposite sign to expectation but its interval spans 0 widely.
caveats: Below 2 atm no analysed test re-ignited (0/86): that wall is reported as a descriptive table, and the logistic model only covers 2-5 atm.
The type-B thermocouple catalytic re-ignition seen in CFI-G (PSI-159) is a different hardware effect; CFI uses no such probe near the droplet.
Farnesane tests are not analysed in the spreadsheet and are absent.
Within 2-5 atm the logistic fit has no skill on held-out days (pressure levels were flown on separate days, and d0, blend and helium add nothing measurable), so only the pressure table is a result.
must_not_be_used_for: pressures below 2 atm via this model (use the table)

models.question: How long is a microgravity co-flow jet flame at its smoke point, for a given nozzle and co-flow speed?
models.target_definition: luminous flame length (mm, video) of run-log rows marked as at the smoke point

features.name: nozzle_mm
features.why: published fit L_SP ~ d^-0.91

features.name: flow_cm_s
features.why: published fit L_SP ~ u_a^0.41: co-flow shortens residence time

training_filter.why: not marked as at the smoke point
no flame length or co-flow
flow_below_sensor_range: co-flow (a feature) unreliable
needs_review: co-flow (a feature) unreliable
flow_missing_los: co-flow (a feature) unreliable

prediction_interval.method: 5th-95th percentile of grouped out-of-fold residuals, added to the prediction
prediction_interval.method_plain: The model is refitted without each group of test days and its error on those days is recorded; the range is the estimate plus the 5th and 95th percentile of those errors.

held_out_coverage.method: nested grouped cross-validation: each held-out day's range is rebuilt from the other days only

models.interpretation: Only in sign. The fitted exponents (nozzle -0.04, co-flow +0.25, both intervals spanning 0) are far from the published L_SP ~ d^-0.91 u_a^0.41, and no fit beats the mean on held-out days. With fuels pooled and 23 rows, the fuel-specific smoke point dominates the scatter. The run-log smoke-point rows do not reproduce the published correlation; the 55-point smoke-point review sheet would be needed.
caveats: Only 23 smoke-point rows with a length in the run log against 52-55 smoke points in the reports; the smoke-point review sheet could not be matched row by row.
Fuels (ethylene, propane, 50/75/100% propylene) are pooled because 23 rows cannot support a fuel term; the smoke point is fuel-specific, so the scatter is large.
Outlet-screen clogging changed the true co-flow for a given anemometer reading between days.
must_not_be_used_for: any prediction: this is a descriptive fit

dropped.reason: The end mode (extinction / disruption / completion) is confounded with needle-coating contamination, which the team blames for disruptions: 46 of 165 tests disrupted in 2009-2010 against 15 of 109 in 2011. Radiative vs diffusive extinction is not labelled in the table; deriving it from D_ext/D0 would put the outcome into the label definition with an arbitrary threshold.
No failed-ignition rows: 'will it burn' (and an LOI) cannot be estimated.
Heptane extinctions mix an early radiative branch (D_ext/D0 > 0.9 in 24 of 56) and a diffusive branch, unlabelled; a single linear model across both is not physically meaningful.

cool_flame is True-or-null. Null rows are not negatives: among analysed tests with cool_flame null, comments describe cool-flame burning (FLEX-1214, 1216, 1229), droplets leaving the field of view, or no ignition (FLEX-1212).

60 of 148 hot-flame K values come from flames that went out with D_ext/D0 > 0.95, where K is fitted over a tiny part of the burn (values down to 0.001 mm²/s). Filtering those out selects on the outcome; keeping them makes K mostly measurement noise.

Only 31 rows are marked True and 66 False (429 null). 'False' lumps flames below the smoke point with flames already past it, so the label is not monotone in flame length and a classifier on length, fuel, nozzle and flow has no physical threshold to learn; 21 of the 66 are Nikon still rows duplicating a video row.
18 test-day rows (several flames each) with no outcome column at all: nothing to model per test.
